parts.text: Which statement correctly finishes the work?

options.text: $8 \times 15$ is already complete, because both factors are whole numbers.
Stop at $8 \times 15$, because $120$ is printed as the starting number.
Keep $8$ as it is and only split $15$, giving $120 = 8 \times 3 \times 5$.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Sameer starts factorising $120$ as $8 \times 15$ and wants a complete prime factorisation.

part_answers.answer: Composite factors must be rewritten until only primes remain; $8$ and $15$ are both composite.

teacher.key_rationale: Prime factorisation continues until every factor is prime: 120=2×2×2×3×5. Leaving composites as “whole numbers” is term substitution. Stopping at the printed 120 is surface capture. Splitting only one composite omits finishing both.
